$comment: AUTHORED, NOT GENERATED — and deliberately NOT a `regen.ts` artifact (#674).
A manifest regenerated from a scan of `out/` would classify every new artifact automatically
and report that as a pass. That is membership-by-location wearing a manifest's clothes, which
is the exact defect this file exists to remove. Same reasoning keeps `token-contract.json` out
of regen: a gate allowed to rewrite what it reads has no memory.
Gated by `packages/engine/lint-payload-manifest.ts`. Adding an emitted artifact FAILS that gate
until a human classifies it here. That friction is the feature.
brandsWhy: Asserted BY NAME, in both directions: a brand in `out/` and not here fails, and a brand here
with no emitted artifacts fails. Brands are DATA — the per-kind rules below cover a new one's
files automatically — but membership is a DECISION, so it is stated rather than discovered.
Same posture as the consumability gate's #635 scope assertion.

payload.why: The brand's token system. Per-mode values live under `$extensions.prism3.modes`, which DTCG defines as ignorable (#609).
The conforming projection's base set — readable by a stock Style Dictionary with no custom code (#609, #642).
One overlay per theme mode. Base + overlay is the projection a conforming consumer resolves.
Per-brand agent metadata. Travels because an ejected repo has no Prism3 MCP to query (#668).

The glyph vocabulary and its path data, generated from `icons/*.svg` through `icon-set.ts` (#833). PAYLOAD because any component projection that renders an icon carries this data with it — a client's ejected button needs the caret. It is a generated MODULE rather than an `out/` tree because `components/icon.ts` imports it and the plugin bundles that import into a sandbox with no filesystem, so it could not be read from disk at runtime. The SVGs beside it are authoring input and are outside this manifest, the same way a brand's design brief is. Licence and provenance: `icons/NOTICE.md` — the set is Remix Icon under its own v1.0 licence, held as a swappable placeholder core, which is what keeps our use inside the licence's `design systems where Icons are a minor component` clause.

ours.why: A Figma file already exists at eject time — usually where the brand came from — and the plugin regenerates variables live. Shipping these would ship a snapshot that goes stale on first regeneration (#674, #678).
A preview surface for inspecting the corpus. Ours, not a client deliverable.
Measures observed-vs-generated gap for a STANDARD-dialect brief. A regression artifact; only brands imported that way have one.
Engine-root report on mode coverage. Ours.
The NB perceptual regression record. Ours.
Describes the engine's own levers to a product agent. Product-facing, not client-facing — a payload agent has no levers to turn.
The corpus of BrandInputs the studio boots from. Ours — a client's own input is a separate, per-brand artifact (#677).
